Andy Robertson believes that strengthening Liverpool's defense will be crucial in supporting Arne Slot as he leads the team in a title challenge during his debut season. The team has kept clean sheets in their first two matches, but they face a tough test against Manchester United on Sunday, where their defense will likely be put under more pressure. Despite solid performances against Ipswich and Brentford, Liverpool knows they must continue to improve at the back to maintain their strong start.

Last season, Liverpool conceded 41 goals in 38 matches on their way to a third-place finish, which was seven more than champions Manchester City and 12 more than runners-up Arsenal. However, early signs under Slot have been encouraging, with two clean sheets in their first two games showing promise for the team's defensive capabilities. Robertson highlighted the importance of maintaining this solid defensive record and limiting opponents' chances, starting with the upcoming match against Manchester United.

Handle P.S. Liverpool's ability to keep clean sheets and limit opposition chances will be crucial in maintaining their title challenge under Slot this season. The team knows that they cannot afford to concede as many chances as they did last season if they want to stay competitive at the top of the table. As they prepare to face Manchester United and other tough opponents after the international break, Liverpool will need to continue their defensive improvements to ensure they can compete with the likes of Arsenal and Manchester City.
